framework.name: UK Operational Resilience (FCA/PRA)
framework.description: UK Financial Sector Operational Resilience framework. Covers FCA PS21/3, PRA SS1/21 (operational resilience — impact tolerances for important business services), FCA PS26/2 / PRA PS7/26 (operational incident and third-party reporting, in force March 2027), and PRA SS2/21 (outsourcing and third-party risk management). UK functional equivalent of DORA for regulated financial entities.

objects.title: Important business services — identification
objects.description: Firms must identify their important business services (IBS) — services that if disrupted could cause harm to consumers or market integrity, or could cause risks to the firm's safety and soundness or insurance policyholder protection.

objects.title: Impact tolerances — setting
objects.description: Firms must set impact tolerances for each IBS — the maximum tolerable level of disruption (expressed as time and/or data loss). Impact tolerances must reflect the point at which disruption begins to cause intolerable harm.

objects.title: Mapping — people, processes, technology, facilities, information
objects.description: Firms must map the people, processes, technology, facilities, and information necessary to deliver each IBS to identify vulnerabilities in their operational resilience.

objects.title: Scenario testing — impact tolerance
objects.description: Firms must carry out scenario testing to identify vulnerabilities and assess their ability to remain within impact tolerances during severe but plausible disruption scenarios. Testing must be documented and reviewed annually.

objects.title: Lessons learned — remediation
objects.description: Firms must identify and implement any changes needed to ensure they remain within impact tolerances during disruption. Lessons learned from incidents and testing must be incorporated into resilience improvements.

objects.title: PRA — governance of operational resilience
objects.description: PRA-regulated firms must ensure their Board and senior management take responsibility for operational resilience. Governance arrangements must include clear ownership of IBS identification, impact tolerance setting, and testing programmes.

objects.title: Outsourcing and third-party risk management
objects.description: PRA expects firms to identify, assess, and manage risks from outsourcing and third-party dependencies. Material outsourcing arrangements require notification to the PRA. Firms must maintain a register of material third-party arrangements.

objects.title: Critical third parties (CTP) — FCA/PRA oversight
objects.description: FCA PS24/16 / PRA PS16/24 (November 2024): The FCA and PRA can designate critical third parties (CTPs) and impose resilience standards on them directly. Firms must cooperate with CTP oversight activities.

objects.title: Operational incident reporting (in force March 2027)
objects.description: FCA PS26/2 / PRA PS7/26 (March 2026, in force March 2027): Firms must report significant operational incidents to the FCA/PRA within defined timelines. Initial notification: as soon as practicable. Intermediate report: within 72 hours. Final report: within 4 weeks.

objects.title: Third-party incident reporting (in force March 2027)
objects.description: FCA PS26/2 / PRA PS7/26: Firms must notify the FCA/PRA when a third party causes or contributes to a significant operational incident. Third-party arrangements must include notification obligations in contracts.

objects.title: Self-assessment — annual documentation
objects.description: Firms must produce and maintain a self-assessment document setting out how they have complied with the policy, including their IBS identification, impact tolerances, mapping, testing results, and any identified vulnerabilities and remediation actions.

objects.title: Deadline — remain within impact tolerances by March 2025
objects.description: Firms were required to have set impact tolerances and completed initial testing by 31 March 2022, and to remain within those impact tolerances during any disruption by 31 March 2025. Ongoing: annual testing and self-assessment required.
